examples.knowledge_point: Finding a Quadratic Polynomial Given a Double Root and a Leading Coefficient
examples.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(x)$ has the double root $x_1=x_2=5,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=1.$ Find $P(x).$
examples.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has the double root ${\color{black}x_1=x_2=5},$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is ${\color{black}a=1},$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})^{2} & =1\cdot {(x-5)}^{2} \\  & ={(x-5)}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(x-5)}^{2} & ={x}^{2}-10x+25.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x) = x^2 - 10x+25.$

feedback.problem: The quadratic polynomial $P(t)$ has roots ${t}_{1}=4,{t}_{2}=3,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $2.$ Find $P(t).$
feedback.worked_solution:
Since our quadratic polynomial has roots ${t}_{1}=4$ and ${t}_{2}=3,$ and the coefficient of the quadratic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(t-{t}_{1})(t-{t}_{2}) & =(2)(t-4)(t-3) \\  & =2(t-4)(t-3)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(t-4)(t-3) & =2({t}^{2}-7t+12) \\  & =2{t}^{2}-14t+24.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(t)=2{t}^{2}-14t+24.$
